prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1160; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a second vehicle that entered the intersection during the cross-traffic phase. Claimant reports a wrist fracture from contact with the door frame and airbag deployment. Police report requested and scene photographs obtained from insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and confirms they are handling the matter directly. Claimant describes the sequence of events consistently with the initial statement and provided the name of the treating urgent care facility. Medical authorization form sent to claimant for signature.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. Responding officer noted both drivers reported a green signal in their favor and recorded contributing factors as disputed. Witness contact listed on report; attempted outreach left a voicemail. Liability currently under investigation pending review of intersection camera footage from the municipality.

Entry 4: Received medical records from the treating facility confirming diagnosis of a distal radius fracture to the claimant's left wrist, with a cast applied and orthopedic follow-up scheduled. Records indicate the claimant has missed several days of work. Wage documentation requested from claimant and employer verification form sent.

Entry 5: Traffic camera footage obtained and reviewed. Footage shows the second vehicle entering on a yellow-to-red transition, which supports the insured's account of the collision. Liability assessment updated to favor insured. Claimant informed by phone that the injury claim is under evaluation and that a settlement offer will follow once the medical treatment status is confirmed.
